sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Foundational Principle 1**: The Award was based on the **'Divide and Rule'** strategy, seeking to isolate the Depressed Classes from the Hindu fold by granting them **separate electorates**.
• **Foundational Principle 2**: It provided for **separate electorates** for Muslims, Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, and Europeans, and extended this to the **Depressed Classes**.
• **Foundational Principle 3**: Gandhi viewed this as a **'diabolical' attempt** to disintegrate the Hindu community and launched a **'fast unto death'** at Yerwada Jail to protest the inclusion of the Depressed Classes.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The Award was a direct outcome of the failure of the Second Round Table Conference to reach a consensus on the minority issue.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Voters of a specific community vote only for candidates of their own community.
Institutionalized communal identity over national identity.
Prelims: Frequently tested as a tool of British colonial policy.
Agreement between Gandhi and Ambedkar; replaced separate electorates with reserved seats.
Compromise to save Gandhi's life and maintain Hindu unity.
Mains: Critical for understanding the evolution of Dalit politics.

items.definition: A system where only members of a specific community can vote for a candidate of that same community, effectively creating political ghettos.
The mechanism adopted in the Poona Pact where all voters vote, but candidates must belong to the reserved community; ensures integration while protecting minority representation.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Yerwada Pact**: The formal name for the Poona Pact signed in September 1932.
• **Harijan Sevak Sangh**: Founded by Gandhi post-Poona Pact to work for the upliftment of the Depressed Classes.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: The tension between political representation and social integration.
• **Solutions**: The Poona Pact served as a template for modern-day reservation policies in the Indian Constitution.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'R-A-P' (Ramsay, Award, Poona).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Ramsay MacDonald announced the Award, which led to the Poona Pact.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Separate Electorates' with 'Reserved Seats'. The Communal Award proposed separate electorates; the Poona Pact replaced them with reserved seats in a joint electorate.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Political Fragmentation' to describe the British intent and 'Social Integration' to describe the Gandhian objective.

keyTakeaways: The Communal Award was a British attempt to weaken the nationalist movement by creating a wedge between the Depressed Classes and the rest of the Hindu community.
The Poona Pact was a landmark compromise that ensured political representation for the Depressed Classes without sacrificing national unity.
The event highlights the ideological divergence between Gandhi (focus on social reform within the fold) and Ambedkar (focus on political empowerment).
